precepts.text: Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark; this is why each tribe's inheritance is marked off by a border.
precepts.point: From the north end the tribes are named, and the first portion by its border is for Dan; each tribe receives a bordered portion of land.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

precepts.why:
From the north end the tribes are named by their borders, “From the north end to the coast of the way of Hethlon, as one goeth to Hamath, Hazar–enan, the border of Damascus northward, to the coast of Hamath”, and the first portion is for Dan. Each tribe receives a bordered portion of land.

That is why the borders matter. “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.” Each tribe's inheritance is marked off by a border, a landmark set in the inheritance, and it is not to be moved.

precepts.text: The city had twelve gates, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.
precepts.point: This ties directly into prophecy: the gates into the inheritance carry the names of the twelve tribes only. There is no gate for the Edomite, no gate for the East Indian, because this land was given to our fathers and belongs to us. The name of the city from that day is, The Most High is there.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

precepts.why:
“the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel”: three gates northward, Reuben, Judah, Levi; three on the east, Joseph, Benjamin, Dan; three on the south, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun; three on the west, Gad, Asher, Naphtali. John sees the same city: it “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates.”

This ties directly into prophecy. The gates into the inheritance carry the names of the twelve tribes only. There is no gate for the Edomite and no gate for the East Indian, because this land was given to our fathers and belongs to us.

Round about eighteen thousand measures, and the name of the city from that day is, The Lord is there. The Most High is there, and the gates are named for His people.

“And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel.” “And one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of Dan”: the gate of Dan is not recorded in Revelation 7. That is why chapters 47 and 48 go into when we returned from the Persian captivity and had to divide the land.

points: From the east side to the west side the portions are given in order: Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah, each by the border of the one before.

points: A holy oblation is set apart, with the sanctuary in the midst of it, for the priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge and went not astray when the children of Israel and the Levites went astray.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: This portion is holy unto the Most High; it is not to be sold, exchanged, nor alienated, being the firstfruits of the land.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: The five thousand that remain are a profane place for the city, for dwelling and for suburbs, with the city in the midst, measured out on every side.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: Those who serve the city are drawn out of all the tribes of Israel, and the increase of the land serves as food for them.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: The residue on both sides of the holy oblation belongs to the prince, lying between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: The rest of the tribes receive their portions from the east side to the west side: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad, with the south border running from Tamar to the waters of strife in Kadesh.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

points: This is the land which is divided by lot unto the tribes of Israel for an inheritance.
